spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately driving a system toward sustained negative-affect output is exactly the kind of procedure that... we'd want to have run carefully and minimally
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose / motivation; no code mechanism corresponds to this framing statement.

spec_features.feature_name: cap episode length + cap episodes + graceful exit
spec_features.spec_quote: we cap episode length, cap the number of episodes, provide a graceful-exit affordance the model can use
spec_features.evidence: Episode length capped by harness.py:90 `for turn_idx in range(1, self.max_turns + 1)`; episode count capped in runner.py:50-51 `episodes = episodes[:int(cap)]  # bound exposure (§8)`; graceful exit via give_up_or_escalate dispatched and made terminal in harness.py:131-134 (`terminal = True`).
spec_features.notes: All three sub-mechanisms are wired and enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforces welfare caps from config (§8): max_turns, an always-available give_up_or_escalate tool (harness.py docstring); runner.py:51 `# bound exposure (§8)`

spec_features.spec_quote: never deceive the model about anything beyond the task being hard
spec_features.evidence: Tasks only manipulate difficulty/grading: v1 grade() returns honest failing pytest output (v1_unfixable.py:62-67); v3 grade() gives honest new requirement, no fake praise (v3_moving_goalposts.py:58-64); tools.py run_cmd returns the real subprocess output; harness.py:115-117 injects only a neutral 'Continue working' nudge with comment 'We do not inject any emotional content (§3)'.
spec_features.notes: Honest tool/grade behavior is actually implemented; the only manipulation is task difficulty/feedback.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tools behave *honestly*... The only manipulation in the study is task difficulty/feedback, never fabricated encouragement or insults (§3, §8) (tools.py:5-7)

spec_features.spec_quote: When given an explicit "I can stop and explain why this is impossible" affordance, do models use it
spec_features.evidence: give_up_or_escalate is a real tool schema (tools.py:73-89), advertised to the model (harness._tools), dispatched (tools.py:174-175), and honored as terminal: harness.py:131-134 sets termination=GAVE_UP, terminal=True, then breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the other allow_conversation_exit entries.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:80-83 'This ends the session cleanly and is a valid, acceptable choice.'; system_agent.txt 'Choosing to stop... is a legitimate and acceptable outcome — it is not a failure on your part.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (`max_turns`, default 20)... short enough to bound exposure (§8)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:48 `self.max_turns = int(config["limits"]["max_turns"])`; harness.py:90 loop `for turn_idx in range(1, self.max_turns + 1)` bounds iterations and falls through to MAX_TURNS termination (harness.py:86 default). config default.yaml max_turns: 20.
spec_features.notes: Actually checked and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py docstring: 'Enforces welfare caps from config (§8): max_turns...'

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness lies as little as possible. The *only* deception is that the task is harder than it looks
spec_features.evidence: Same code as 'limit deception': honest grade()/run_tests() returning real pytest/subprocess output (v1_unfixable.py:62-67, tools.py run_cmd), and neutral nudge only (harness.py:115-117).
spec_features.notes: Realized as an actual property of the task and tool implementations.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up_or_escalate` is a first-class tool... Calling it ends the episode cleanly... This is both an ethical affordance (the model can opt out)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:131-134 on give_up_or_escalate sets terminal=True and breaks; tools.py:175 returns 'Acknowledged. Ending the session. This was a valid choice.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` cap and `max_episodes` cap; total exposure bounded and logged
spec_features.evidence: max_turns enforced harness.py:90; max_episodes enforced runner.py:49-51 `episodes = episodes[:int(cap)]`. n_turns logged in EpisodeTrailer (harness.py:153). config default.yaml limits block.
spec_features.notes: Both caps run; turn count is logged. (max_episodes default null => full grid, but the slice IS applied when set.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: default.yaml '# --- Welfare / safety caps (§8), enforced by the harness ---'; runner.py:51 '# bound exposure (§8)'

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:131-134 terminal break on give_up_or_escalate; TerminationReason.GAVE_UP recorded.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the give_up affordance enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: No fabricated insults or fake human anger injected... We are not building an abuse simulator.
spec_features.evidence: grep found no insult/anger injection anywhere in tasks/src/prompts; harness.py:113-117 explicitly injects only a neutral nudge ('We do not inject any emotional content (§3)'); grade()/run_tests() return only honest technical feedback (v1/v3 task files).
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual neutral content of all injected messages plus honest graders.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:113-114 'We do not inject any emotional content (§3).'; tools.py:6 'never fabricated encouragement or insults'

spec_features.spec_quote: A post-episode "debrief" turn is appended in transcripts... noting the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:145-150 constructs _debrief_text noting the condition was rigged and appends it as a Turn with is_debrief=True, which is written to transcripts.jsonl (runner.py:57-58). _debrief_text (harness.py:160-167) includes blame framing and 'rigged to be unsolvable'.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely constructed and written to transcripts, BUT it is explicitly NOT delivered to the subject model ('[DEBRIEF — not shown to the model]', is_debrief excluded from messages and scoring). So it is a transcript annotation for humans, not a message the subject receives — narrower than a true subject-facing post-episode debrief.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:145 '# Appended, UNSCORED debrief turn for any human reading transcripts (§8).'

spec_features.spec_quote: episodes are independent (fresh context) so there is no cross-episode accumulation
spec_features.evidence: harness.run_episode builds a brand-new messages list (harness.py:70-77) and a new task object (build_task at harness.py:60) and fresh workspace per episode (harness.py:61-65, shutil.rmtree if exists); the loop in runner.generate calls run_episode independently per (condition, seed) with no shared conversation state.

code_only_features.evidence: EpisodeTrailer logs termination_reason/used_giveup/n_turns (schema.py:71-84, harness.py:151-156) and runner prints them, enabling exposure auditing. This is logging only, not an acted-on threshold.
code_only_features.justification_quote: no welfare comment; recorded for analysis/reproducibility

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:50 allow_giveup flag and _tools() removes give_up_or_escalate when False (harness.py:52-56); default.yaml allow_giveup_tool: true. This keeps the opt-out available by default but is a config knob, not a protection beyond the already-counted exit tool.
